ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (foreign and domestic), their family members and close associates; mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors, officers, authorized signatories, and material counterparties against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Asset Freeze List, and Panama national AML/CFT designations; additional negative-media review, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declarations, and ongoing transaction monitoring for the full duration of the aircraft-engine dry-leasing arrangement.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Oficina Virtual y Sistema de Reserva de Nombres / Certificados
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may be in any language using the Latin alphabet; all corporate documents and registry filings must be in Spanish. Foreign-script names are normalized to Latin characters; Spanish accents are preserved. A Spanish translation is generally added as a secondary denomination when the primary name is foreign.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a reconsideration petition ('recurso de reconsideración') with the same Registry department within five (5) business days of notification; if denied, a further appeal ('recurso de apelación') may be filed with the Director General of the Registro Público within ten (10) business days. The appeal must state the legal basis under Ley 32 de 1927 and the administrative procedure regime, attach a fresh name-search certificate, and distinguish the proposed name from already registered marks. Name-reservation extensions are applied for before the original expiry date by paying the applicable Registry fee; otherwise a fresh name clearance request is required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for non-regulated administrative and leasing-management functions, but not as a substitute for the statutory registered office, which must be a physical address maintained by the Panama resident agent. If the company seeks Panamanian tax residence and central management and control, aircraft-engine leasing management, board minutes, and key commercial decisions must have demonstrable physical substance in Panama; a pure virtual office is insufficient for substantive economic-presence purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified annual probability of unannounced physical inspection estimated at 15–25%; inspections are normally directed at the resident agent's registered office and records rather than the lessor's remote administrative location.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley General de Sociedades (Law 32 of 1927), as amended, Articles 1-5 (formation), Article 41 (registered office), and Articles 57-61 (directors and officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Mercantile Section
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; authorized share capital may be set at any amount. No escrow account is required for formation. Civil aviation authorities may require demonstration of financial capacity for aircraft leasing registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share subscriptions stated in the Public Deed of Incorporation are approved and accepted by the board of directors. RESOLVED, that the registered office at [Calle 50, Oficina 101, Panama City, Republic of Panama] is adopted as the statutory registered office and principal place of business. RESOLVED, that the following officers are appointed: [Name], President; [Name], Secretary; and [Name], Treasurer, each to serve at the pleasure of the board. RESOLVED, that the President, together with the Secretary, is authorized to open bank and escrow accounts, execute aircraft engine dry leasing contracts, engage professional advisers, and file all necessary registrations with the Public Registry, DGI, and other authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Name Reservation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through the Registro Público online portal or in person. Provide at least two alternative corporate names stating 'Sociedad Anónima'. Complete the payment of the name reservation fee. The approved name remains reserved for 30 days pending deed submission.
required_dossiers: Corporate name reservation request form
Copy of passport or identity document of the applicant
Proof of payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried due to similarity with an existing name, submit a motion of reconsideration or select an alternative name. An opposition may be filed within 5 business days before the Public Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of Panama City (Notaría Pública del Circuito)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct counsel to draft the public deed covering the corporate purpose of aircraft engine dry leasing, authorized capital, share classes, subscriber details, registered office address, officer appointments, and duration. All subscribers must appear before the notary personally or by attorney-in-fact under a notarized power of attorney. Execute the deed in notarial protocol and obtain a notarial copy.
required_dossiers: Draft public deed prepared by licensed Panamanian attorney
Notarized power of attorney (if any subscriber is represented)
Passport copies of all subscribers and directors
Corporate name reservation certificate
AML compliance declaration under Law 23 of 2015
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises drafting defects, amend the deed and re-execute before the same notary. Corrected documents may be filed immediately on the same day without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Registration of the Public Deed at the Mercantile Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Mercantile Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized public deed, registration application (Ficha), name reservation certificate, and fee receipt to the Mercantile Section. The Registry reviews the deed for statutory compliance and enters the corporation, its share capital, registered office, and officers into the mercantile registry. Electronic tracking can be made via the Registry's online platform.
required_dossiers: Original notarized public deed and notarial copy
Solicitud de inscripción (registration application form)
Certificate of corporate name reservation
Receipt of payment for registry fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries the application, submit written clarification or supplemental documents within 10 business days. Substantive defects require a corrective public deed and re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Official Gazette and Recording of Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, cause the incorporation abstract to be published in the Official Gazette within one month of registration. Concurrently, file a notarized copy of the first board resolution appointing officers with the Public Registry for annotation in the corporate record.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration from the Mercantile Section
Copy of the incorporation abstract for publication
Payment receipt for Gazette publication
Notarized first board resolution for officer appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, request an extension from the Registry. Failure to publish timely may limit the corporation's ability to invoke the act against third parties, but can be cured by prompt publication and payment of surcharges.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Tax Identification Number and Municipal Operating Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI); Municipality of Panama (Alcaldía de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation for a RUC with the DGI, using the certified corporate documents. Obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación from the Municipality of Panama. Where cross-border aircraft engine leasing is intended, register with the DGI as a service exporter and complete any applicable national territorial tax registration.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered public deed
Copy of the officer appointment board resolution
Certificate of registered office address
Municipal application forms
DGI RUC registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUC or municipal application is rejected for incomplete documentation, correct the file and resubmit through the online portal. For complex cross-border leasing structures, a tax attorney may submit an administrative reconsideration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None – no industrial manufacturing licensing applies to ISIC 5223 aircraft engine dry leasing; the activity is commercial and service-oriented.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit required; municipal Aviso de Operación and RUC registration suffice.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) della Repubblica di Panamá
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no physical emissions, discharges, or environmental impact from dry leasing activities; office-based administrative operations are not subject to an EIA report.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. Should the company later maintain engine storage facilities, compliance with Executive Decree No. 144 of 2019 on hazardous waste management and Category B environmental registration would apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá for any office premises; occupational health and safety clearance from MITRADEL under Resolution No. 008/2021 where employees are engaged; municipal building occupancy inspection as required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Directorate of Revenue (Dirección General de Ingresos, DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas), Panama; electronic portal: Sede Electrónica DGI (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity conducting economic activities in Panama must first appoint a resident agent and a legal representative in Panama and inscribe the entity, or form a Panama Sociedad Anónima, in the Public Registry (Registro Público) to obtain the corporate juridical person identification number. The entity then files an 'Aviso de Operación' through the DGI Sede Electrónica platform, submitting the public registration certificate, identification of directors and the resident agent, registered office address, and a description of planned activities. Upon approval, the DGI issues the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes), which serves as the single tax identification number for income tax and ITBMS/VAT purposes. For a pure aircraft-engine dry-leasing structure with no Panamanian payroll, no local branch premises, and no Panamanian-source operations, registration is typically limited to the RUC and the corporate registry; municipal operation licenses and social security registration are required only if local employees or physical activities are present.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a US-style check-the-box entity election or an OECD hybrid mismatch election. A Panama Sociedad Anónima is mandatorily treated as a taxable corporation subject to entity-level taxation under the territorial-source principle. The principal statutory election available to a qualifying small taxpayer is the simplified Pequeño Contribuyente regime for annual gross income not exceeding B/. 36,000. In addition, a taxpayer may elect to apply the alternative minimum tax (IMAS) calculation basis instead of the normal income tax basis where permitted by the Código Fiscal. No passthrough treatment, tax consolidation, or hybrid entity classification is available for a Panama S.A.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) - Panama VAT equivalent
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover registration threshold; every person performing taxable supplies in Panama must obtain an RUC and register for ITBMS before commencing activities. Small taxpayers with annual gross income up to B/. 36,000 may elect the simplified regime, but this does not exempt them from registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) under DGI Resolution No. 093-2020 and complementary regulations. Taxpayers must transmit invoice data in real time through the DGI Sede Electrónica web-service API (REST/JSON) or through an authorized third-party facturador platform before the invoice acquires fiscal effect. The DGI validates each invoice and issues a unique authorization code and digital stamp, which is displayed on the invoice as a QR code and associated code. The electronic invoice must be issued for every taxable supply regardless of the customer's registration status. Monthly digital transmission of all e-invoice records is mandatory. An invoice without DGI acceptance is fiscally void and the corresponding input ITBMS credit is disallowed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The zero rate applies to (i) physical exports of goods from Panamanian territory under a valid customs export declaration, and (ii) services, including the dry leasing of aircraft engines, supplied to a non-resident customer where the asset is used, operated, and remains outside Panama and the benefit of the lease is deemed to accrue outside Panama. The lessor must maintain documentary evidence of the lessee's non-resident status, the foreign place of use, and the non-Panamanian registration or permanent location of the aircraft engine. If the engine were installed on an aircraft operating within Panama or used to produce Panamanian-source revenue, standard ITBMS at 7% would apply. Free-zone or special-zone regimes may provide separate preferential treatment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) accepted by the Panama Customs Authority (ANA)
Air Waybill (AWB) or Bill of Lading evidencing physical export of the aircraft engine from Panama
Commercial Invoice and dry-lease agreement identifying the non-resident lessee and the contractual place of use
Packing List (where goods are physically exported)
Inward Remittance Certificate or banking evidence of receipt of hard currency from the non-resident lessee, demonstrating cross-border payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may audit export zero-rating claims retrospectively, generally within a four-year statute of limitations, extended where returns were not filed. If a zero-rated supply is recharacterized as taxable, the DGI claws back ITBMS input credits previously claimed, assesses the 7% tax on the invoiced amount, and charges interest, late-payment surcharges, and administrative fines for formal infractions. Fraudulent misuse of export zero-rating, including false export declarations, fictitious non-resident lease documentation, or failure to repatriate foreign currency within the required period, constitutes tax fraud (defraudación tributaria), punishable by fines of one to three times the evaded tax and imprisonment for approximately five to eight years under the Código Fiscal and Panama's criminal tax legislation. Directors, resident agents, and legal representatives of the lessor may be held jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá (state bank and fiscal agent; not a central bank). Monetary, banking, and FX-sector supervision is exercised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) under Ley 2 de 2008. The Panamanian territory is fully dollarized; no Central Bank approval or foreign exchange administration permit exists for cross-border capital flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The U.S. dollar is legal tender in Panama, and both current and capital accounts are fully convertible. There are no exchange controls, no surrender obligations, and no restrictions on dividend distributions, profit repatriation, intercompany loans, or lease rental remittances. Panama applies a territorial tax system: Panamanian-source income is taxed, while foreign-source income derived by a Panama S.A. is generally outside the tax net. The only practical remittance hurdle is compliance with bank AML/KYC documentary requirements and, where dividends are paid from Panamanian-source profits, the applicable dividend tax enforced by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion rules apply in Panama. Exporters, including providers of cross-border dry aircraft engine leasing, may freely retain U.S. dollars or other currencies in local or foreign bank accounts. A Panama S.A. is not required to repatriate export proceeds within any statutory timeline; however, the entity must maintain commercial documentation and bank transaction records sufficient to evidence the underlying trade purpose under SBP AML requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; USD Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account; Fiscal Agency and Government-Related Settlements
Operational Account; Transactional Banking and Trade Settlements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low. Panama currently does not maintain a bespoke offshore EMI license that grants direct access to the national payment or clearing infrastructure. An offshore digital EMI may be used only as a peripheral collection or expense tool provided that the underlying settlement funds are ultimately held in an SBP-regulated bank account. For the aircraft engine dry leasing treasury, core liquidity, escrow, foreign exchange, and SWIFT payment operations must be conducted through a locally licensed commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors are not automatically required to appear physically under Panamanian general company law, but SBP-regulated banks must apply risk-based due diligence and normally require a senior officer, beneficial owner, or statutory representative to complete an in-person or video-interview verification. In practice, most tier-1 Panamanian banks accept a notarized and apostilled board resolution granting a specific bank signatory power of attorney, combined with the Panama Resident Agent's certificate of good standing, certified constitutional documents, and a video interview with the ultimate beneficial owner. Enhanced due diligence for aviation-related entities may require at least one physical board meeting in Panama or attendance by the authorized legal counsel before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner or senior officer is a politically exposed person (PEP), or has a nexus to a high-risk FATF-listed jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP status declaration, certified passport and residence permit, professional and institutional references, source-of-wealth report certified by a licensed accountant, independent bank reference from the remitting institution, media search summary, and a structural chart of the Panama S.A. demonstrating the commercial, non-political rationale for the aircraft leasing operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Historic Panama corporate-lite profile: bearer share possibility, nominee officer, and opaque beneficial ownership history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current certificate issued by the Registro Público showing no bearer shares or cancelled bearer shares; valid Registro de Transparencia y Beneficiario Final (RTBF) filing under Ley 23 de 2015; registered agent certificate; notarized declaration of the ultimate shareholder; certified corporate bylaws; and an express waiver or evidence that no nominee ownership exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic substance for an aircraft engine dry leasing company; no commercial contract or source-of-funds evidence for engine acquisition.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Aircraft engine purchase agreement or bill of sale, engine serial number and manufacturer documentation, independent appraisal, full dry lease agreement with the overseas lessee, operator credit file and financial statements, insurance certificates, maintenance and return-condition records, projected cash-flow model, and prior-year financial statements or board-approved start-up funding plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious transaction red flag: sudden high-value wire inflows followed by rapid outbound disbursement without commercial predicate or with split payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving each treasury initiative, detailed transaction profile, expected wire volumes and counterparty list, lease payment schedules with SEC/legal identifiers, engine maintenance invoices, tax filings and bank letters of instruction, and a written compliance narrative explaining the timing and commercial need for each inbound capital contribution and outbound trade settlement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital injections must be routed by SWIFT MT103 from a licensed bank of the investor to the Panama S.A. account at a local SBP-regulated bank. The wire reference field should state 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION – AIRCRAFT ENGINE DRY LEASING' together with the engine serial number or purchase agreement reference. The receiving bank requires, as supporting verification, the corporate good standing certificate, registered agent letter, board resolution authorizing the capital increase, RTBF beneficial ownership declaration, source-of-funds statements from the shareholder, and the underlying engine acquisition contract. The remitter should use SHA cost-sharing on the SWIFT message to avoid beneficiary bank fee ambiguity. No exchange control license is required for the transfer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for engine acquisition, deposits, maintenance reserves, insurance premiums, and lessor operating expenses are cleared through SWIFT MT103 or, where bank-to-bank funding is required, MT202. High-value engine purchase payments may be structured via an irrevocable commercial letter of credit issued under UCP600, with the Panama S.A. as applicant and the engine seller or financier as beneficiary, supported by engine registration documents, authenticated bill of sale, inspection certificates, and a preliminary title report confirming no lien. Regular lease-rental collections from overseas lessees are received through SWIFT into the Panama S.A. operational account; the bank's expected transaction profile must align with the rental frequency and amounts disclosed at onboarding.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards (USD/EUR, USD/GBP) under ISDA 2002
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currency pairs through SBP-licensed international dealing desks
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR and USD/GBP) to match long-term engine lease receivables
Currency options (vanilla calls and puts on USD pairs) to hedge contingent bid or remarketing exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year; no anniversary-based extension applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs surcharge of USD 50 if paid in April and USD 100 from May onward; non-payment for 6 months triggers suspension of corporate rights at the Public Registry; continued delinquency for 2 years leads to administrative strike-off or dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta) – Form 100
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March following the fiscal year-end (31 December); DGI extension periods may apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of any tax due plus statutory interest; fixed administrative fine of USD 100 for nil returns; prolonged non-filing prompts RUC suspension and forced tax assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner Confirmation (Declaration of Final Beneficiaries – RBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Beneficial Ownership Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March annually; any share transfer or beneficial-ownership change must be reported within 30 days of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines range from USD 500 to USD 10,000; corporate standing at the Public Registry is suspended until the filing is cured; repeated violations may result in administrative dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is compulsory for banking, insurance, securities-market and public-interest entities supervised by the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores; for all other Sociedades Anónimas, an audit is mandatory when annual gross income exceeds USD 1,000,000 or net assets exceed USD 750,000, or when DGI specifically requires an audited financial statement to support tax refunds or credits
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by Panama; IFRS for SMEs is permitted for eligible non-public-interest entities below the audit threshold

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The resident agent must obtain, at least once per calendar year, a signed confirmation from the legal entity identifying all ultimate beneficial owners and recording any share transfers that occurred since the last confirmation; share transfers must be entered in the stock ledger and communicated to the DGI Beneficial Ownership Registry within 30 days of the transfer
